Tomasz: Hello, hello, can you hear me okay? Ollie, yeah?
Ollie: Yeah, hi, I can hear you fine. Tomasz, is it?
Tomasz: Tomasz, yeah, perfect. So how was the puzzle thing, you finished it? I done it quite fast, to be honest.
Ollie: Erm, I got most of them. There was one with the shapes that kind of broke my brain a bit, but yeah, fine.
Tomasz: Yeah, the shapes, that one was bit annoying. So what do you do, Ollie? You look like, I don't know, city guy, consultant or something.
Ollie: Ha, no, I wish. I'm a student actually, second year at King's, doing geography. I do Saturdays at a running shop by London Bridge as well, so that's the job bit.
Tomasz: Ah. Student. Okay. Geography, so like maps and rivers and stuff?
Ollie: Kind of, yeah, but I'm more on the human side, so cities, transport, how people get around. My dissertation's probably going to be on cycling infrastructure, like who actually uses the cycle lanes and who doesn't. I'm trying to get an internship in transport planning this summer, TfL or one of the big consultancies, Arup, AECOM, that kind of thing.
Tomasz: Cycle lanes. Mate, I sell cars. You're basically my enemy.
Ollie: Oh no. What kind of cars?
Tomasz: Premium German, in Park Royal. New and approved used. Saturday I sold three, one of them proper spec, like ninety grand car. And you want to put cycle lane outside my showroom, yeah?
Ollie: I mean, not outside your showroom specifically. Probably not on the A40.
Tomasz: Good, good. To be fair, I'm not against it. Central line is a nightmare, everybody needs to get to work somehow. But people who buy from me, they're not getting a bike, you know what I mean.
Ollie: No, that's fair. It's more about the short trips. Loads of car journeys in London are under a couple of miles. That's the stuff you could actually swap.
Tomasz: Mm. Maybe. You look like you're into fitness anyway. You run?
Ollie: Yeah, loads. Burgess Park parkrun most Saturdays. Nineteen forty's my PB, which I'm, yeah, quite pleased with.
Tomasz: Nineteen forty, that's good, that's good. I don't run, I'm more weights. Four mornings a week, gym on Ealing Broadway. Bench is hundred and twenty at the moment.
Ollie: Hundred and twenty kilos? That's a lot.
Tomasz: Yeah, it's okay. I want one forty before summer. But after six it's impossible, the gym is full of kids filming themselves.
Ollie: Ha, yeah. I'd get crushed under that, honestly. My legs are fine, my arms are kind of decorative.
Tomasz: You need to come to gym, mate. So after the degree, the TfL thing, money is not great there, no?
Ollie: Probably not amazing to start, no. But I quite like the idea of working on how cities get people out of cars, so—
Tomasz: Out of cars! See, again.
Ollie: Sorry, sorry, I'll stop. Do you follow football at all?
Tomasz: Arsenal. Since 2009, my flatmates were Arsenal so, yeah. You?
Ollie: Watford. Mostly because of my dad. It's not been a fun season.
Tomasz: Watford. Okay. Hard life, mate.
Ollie: Yeah, it's character building, that's what I tell myself. Do you play?
Tomasz: Five-a-side sometimes with guys from work. They're useless, honestly. Same guys who don't hit target on the sales floor, they don't run on the pitch either.
Ollie: Ha. I play Wednesdays, it's a mix of course mates. Honestly, we're not much better.
Tomasz: We should do a game, dealership against students. We'd destroy you.
Ollie: I reckon we'd outrun you, to be fair.
Tomasz: Running, yeah, but we'd just—

=== CALL C0476 ===
Gareth: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
Darren: Yeah, hiya. Darren.
Gareth: Gareth. Nice to meet you.
Darren: And you. Did you get through that puzzle alright?
Gareth: Yeah, got through it. Couple I wasn't sure about. You?
Darren: Same. Ran out of time on the last one, to be fair.
Gareth: Whereabouts are you, then?
Darren: Stourbridge. You sound local-ish.
Gareth: Shirley, Solihull. Grew up in Acocks Green, though.
Darren: Ah, right. Not far, then.
Gareth: No. What do you do?
Darren: Gas engineer. Heating firm in Halesowen, mostly boilers. Servicing, repairs, replacements, that sort of thing.
Gareth: Busy this time of year, I'd imagine.
Darren: Yeah, no, it's been mad. Winter's always the worst, everyone's boiler packs up the first cold week. Had one yesterday, eight years old, heat exchanger gone. People don't get them serviced, they think it's a waste of money, then they're ringing Sunday night with no hot water and two kids in the house. And half the time it's a cheap unit someone's fitted badly to start with, so you're sort of fixing somebody else's job as well.
Gareth: Yeah. We see a bit of that. Different scale.
Darren: What is it you do?
Gareth: Quantity surveyor. Senior Commercial Manager at a contractor in Birmingham, hospitals and schools mainly. I look after the money side. Cost reports, valuations, subcontractor accounts, you know.
Darren: Right. So you're the one telling people they're not getting paid what they asked for.
Gareth: Pretty much, yeah. Politely.
Darren: Ha. I've got a mate does the M&E side on them big jobs, he moans about QSs all the time.
Gareth: They all do. Then they ring me when they want paying early.
Darren: Do you have much to do with heat pumps on your jobs? Everyone keeps telling me I've got to do the training.
Gareth: Er, yeah, on the new schools mostly. Air source. Spec's all heading that way now, so... I'd do it, if I were you. Work's going there whether anyone likes it or not.
Darren: Yeah. I know. I just don't trust them yet in a seventies semi with no insulation, you know. You put one in, it's not keeping up, and who's the customer ringing? Me.
Gareth: That's fair.
Darren: You got kids?
Gareth: Two. Oliver's eleven, Isla's eight. You?
Darren: Two as well. Ellie's fifteen, Jack's twelve. Wife's Claire.
Gareth: Sorry, say that again?
Darren: Wife's called Claire.
Gareth: So's mine.
Darren: Get away.
Gareth: Honestly. Claire. Part-time, in HR.
Darren: Mine's part-time on reception at a dentist. That's a bit weird, that.
Gareth: Must be the area. Football?
Darren: Baggies. Always have been.
Gareth: Blues.
Darren: Oh dear. Well, we'll not fall out over it. Still go?
Gareth: Half-season share with a mate. Don't make as many as I should. Owners don't help.
Darren: No, we've had our share of that an' all. I get to a few with my brother-in-law, rest is on the radio in the van.
Gareth: Not a bad way to do it. You can turn it off when they're losing.
Darren: That's about it really.
Gareth: Booked next year's holiday yet? I've done ours already. January's when the deals are.
Darren: Same caravan park near Tenby, every summer. Booked it the week we got back.
Gareth: Can't beat knowing what you're getting.
Darren: That's what I keep telling Claire.
Gareth: Which one?
Darren: Ha. Either, probably.

Rhys: Classic! Is he working today?
